topic: How to learn anything in half the time
themes_scanned: TED: Josh Kaufman — learning a skill in 20 hours (trend signal: public appetite for speed-learning)
TED: Tim Ferriss — fear-setting (signals: high tolerance for counterintuitive learning claims)

primary_sources.title: Über das Gedächtnis: Untersuchungen zur experimentellen Psychologie (Memory: A Contribution to Experimental Psychology)
primary_sources.author: Hermann Ebbinghaus
primary_sources.how_used: Establishes the biological urgency of early reinforcement—the decay curve defines the optimal timing windows for each principle in the Compound Retention System.

primary_sources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
primary_sources.author: Henry L. Roediger III and Jeffrey D. Karpicke
primary_sources.how_used: Supports Principle 2 (Productive Friction)—effortful recall acts as the compounding mechanism that strengthens memory traces beyond passive review.

primary_sources.title: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
primary_sources.author: Peter C. Brown, Henry L. Roediger III, and Mark A. McDaniel
primary_sources.how_used: Provides the pedagogical backbone for Principle 3 (Contextual Bridging)—connecting new material to existing knowledge structures multiplies retrieval routes.

primary_sources.title: The Spacing and Interleaving Effects in Learning: Practice Is Not Enough
primary_sources.author: Nate Kornell and Robert A. Bjork
primary_sources.how_used: Underpins Principle 1 (Layered Encoding)—mixing related concepts during a single session forces the brain to differentiate and categorize, creating richer initial memory traces.

primary_sources.title: Enhancing Human Learning via Spaced Repetition Optimization
primary_sources.author: Tabibian, Upadhyay, De, Zarezade, Schölkopf & Gomez-Rodriguez
primary_sources.how_used: Evidence that AI-driven spacing outperforms uniform schedules; grounds the Layered Encoding amplification claim

primary_sources.title: Using AI to Implement Effective Teaching Strategies in Classrooms: Five Strategies, Including Prompts
primary_sources.author: Mollick & Mollick
primary_sources.how_used: Direct evidence for Productive Friction layer; shows LLMs operationalize retrieval practice and elaborative interrogation

primary_sources.title: ChatGPT for Good? On Opportunities and Challenges of Large Language Models for Education
primary_sources.author: Kasneci, Seßler, Küchemann, Bannert, Dementieva, Fischer et al.
primary_sources.how_used: Supports the overall AI Amplification Layer thesis and the AI-only principle of real-time knowledge-state modeling

original_framework.name: The Compound Retention System
original_framework.updated_thesis: Long-term retention is the product of biologically-grounded learning principles (spacing, retrieval, interleaving) multiplied by AI execution infrastructure that personalizes timing, manufactures friction, and bridges context—turning sporadic professional study into a continuously-optimizing retention engine

layer_1.name: Traditional Methods (Biology)
layer_1.description: Traditional methods (biology) — why retention works: forgetting curves, retrieval strengthening, interleaved discrimination

principles.name: Layered Encoding
principles.ai_role: AI generates multi-modal restatements of the same concept—summaries, analogies, quiz questions, diagrams-as-code—automatically creating the encoding variability that strengthens memory traces without the professional needing to manually rephrase material

principles.name: Productive Friction
principles.ai_role: AI withholds direct answers and instead poses Socratic follow-ups, generates increasingly difficult retrieval questions calibrated to the learner's error patterns, and forces explanation before revealing solutions—manufacturing desirable difficulty on demand

principles.name: Contextual Bridging
principles.ai_role: AI maps new concepts onto the learner's existing professional domain by generating domain-specific examples, case studies, and application scenarios drawn from their stated work context, accelerating transfer from abstract knowledge to workplace use

layer_2.name: AI Amplification (Execution)
layer_2.description: AI amplification (execution) — how retention scales: personalized scheduling, Socratic generation, domain-mapped transfer, and real-time knowledge-state modeling

ai_only_principle.name: Real-Time Knowledge-State Modeling
ai_only_principle.explanation: AI continuously infers what the learner knows, partially knows, and has forgotten by analyzing response latency, error patterns, and confidence signals across sessions—building a dynamic model of memory strength that no static system or self-assessment can replicate. This enables micro-targeted interventions at the exact threshold of forgetting.
ai_only_principle.example: A professional studying AWS architecture gets quizzed on VPC peering on Tuesday because the AI's model predicts that specific concept has decayed to 60% recall probability—while skipping IAM policies entirely because confidence signals remain strong. No manual scheduling required.

originality_check.note: The Compound Retention System focuses on HOW interactions transform knowledge, not WHEN. Distinct from spaced repetition (timing-only) and Feynman Technique (single modality).
